function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just a convenient delivery option.

---

## 1️⃣ Local Bakeries & Specialty Shops  
These places often offer fresh, made‑to‑order cakes and can accommodate custom designs.

| Platform / Service | What to Look For | Tips |
|--------------------|------------------|------|
| **Google Maps / Yelp** | Search “cake shop near me” or “custom bakery” | Check recent reviews, photos, and ratings. |
| **Local Facebook Groups / Nextdoor** | Community recommendations | Ask neighbors for their favorite spots. |
| **Bakery Websites** | Online ordering forms, menu PDFs | Many bakeries now let you upload a photo of your design idea. |

### How to Order:
1. Visit the bakery’s website or call them directly.  
2. Choose size, flavor, and any special decorations.  
3. Provide delivery address and preferred pickup time.  
4. Pay online or over the phone (most accept credit cards, Venmo, or cash).  

---

## 2️⃣ Big‑Name Delivery Apps  
If you want convenience and a wide selection, try one of these apps:

| App | Strengths | Typical Price Range |
|-----|-----------|---------------------|
| **Uber Eats** | Fast delivery, many partner restaurants | $10–$30 per cake |
| **DoorDash** | Good for larger orders, frequent promos | $12–$35 per cake |
| **Postmates** | Flexible delivery windows, good for last‑minute needs | $15–$40 per cake |
| **Instacart** | Grocery + bakery items, same‑day delivery | $8–$25 per cake |

> **Pro Tip:** Use promo codes or free delivery offers when available. Some apps give you a discount if you’re a new user or if you order during off‑peak hours.

---

## 3️⃣ Online Specialty Cake Stores  
For premium or themed cakes, consider dedicated cake sites.

| Site | Highlights | Cost |
|------|------------|------|
| **Goldbelly** | Nationwide delivery from top bakeries | $50–$200+ depending on size & shipping |
| **CakeBoss** | Custom designs, seasonal flavors | $20–$60 per cake |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, artisanal cakes from independent bakers | $25–$70 per cake |

> **Tip:** Etsy sellers often allow you to customize the design via messages; check shipping policies carefully.

---

## 4️⃣ Grocery Store Chains  
Many supermarkets have in‑house bakeries that ship or deliver.

| Chain | Delivery Options | Notes |
|-------|------------------|-------|
| **Whole Foods** | Same‑day delivery via Amazon Prime | Great for organic ingredients |
| **Walmart** | In‑store pickup or delivery via Walmart+ | Budget friendly |
| **Kroger** | Delivery through Kroger Delivery or Instacart | Often has loyalty discounts |

---

## 5️⃣ DIY & Pre‑Made Options  
If you’re short on time or budget, consider pre‑made cakes that still taste great.

| Option | Where to Buy | Why It Works |
|--------|--------------|--------------|
| **Frozen Cakes** | Costco, Sam’s Club | Bulk savings, long shelf life |
| **Pre‑Baked Cupcakes** | Target, Walmart | Easy to transport, no baking required |
| **Custom Cake Boxes** | Amazon, Walmart | Ready‑to‑serve, often includes frosting |

---

## Quick Checklist Before You Order

1. **Confirm Delivery Time** – Make sure the cake arrives when you need it.  
2. **Check Reviews** – Look at recent customer photos and comments.  
3. **Ask About Allergens** – Especially important if you’re ordering for a group.  
4. **Verify Payment Methods** – Some bakeries only accept certain payment types.  
5. **Read Cancellation Policy** – Know how far in advance you can cancel without penalty.

---

### Final Thought  
The best choice depends on your priorities: freshness vs. convenience, customization vs. cost, or local charm vs. nationwide reach. Try a mix of local bakeries for personalized touches and delivery apps for quick, reliable service. Happy cake hunting! 🍰
